I arrived onsite and checked in with the front office. I set up my extension ladder and gained access to the rooftop. I found the unit was not controlling the VFD. After diagnosing the issue I found the wire for the VFD signal had come loose on the drive. This was caused by the wire being too tight. I was able to get slack in the wire. I set up the unit to run in CV VFD to allow the fan to ramp up and down. I verified the unit would ramp the VFD up and down.
Found main base board output to a-2 compressor bad. Ordered new main base board.  Replaced main base board. Reconfigured and checked operation.

Found hot gas line cracked on joint at discharge header, will need new drier and 47# of R 410A. Also other unit serial number should be 1819U49354 not 1819U49353    Repair leak at hot gas stub and evacuate to 490 microns. Add 40# of R410A to circuit A.

Unit was off and in alarm. Found low return air temp alarm and low saturated suction temp alarm. Reset and both circuits started up. Found HOA switch for cooling stage 1 and 2 set to hand. Set back to auto. After running for a little while it tripped again on low saturated suction temp. Put in test mode and tried to run supply fan. It did not come on. Pulled panel and found display for VFD blank. Checked to make sure power was at VFD and had it. Pulled display out of another unit and tested. Fan came on. Will order new display for VFD.  Had to get more info for warranty. Shut down unit and removed access panel for VFD. Got info from VFD to order new display. Put panel back on and turned unit back on.  Replaced bad display for VFD. Tested out and checked unit operation. Left running.
